releases.author: LiveAQuietLife
releases.description:
## [1.0.5] - 2026-07-26

### Fixed
- The dashboard empty state asked you to add your first "list" (or whatever your collection term was set to) instead of your first book. It now says book, because that's what the button below it does.
- The Add book confirm step and the dashboard had two different methods both named `formatDate` that produced different output. The long form is now named `formatDateLong` and delegates to the shared helper.
- Long titles or author names could push the status badge out of place on dashboard book cards.

### Changed
- Custom collection terms now have separate plural and singular fields. Verso uses the singular in most places and the plural in a few, and inferring one from the other got English wrong too often. Existing custom terms are kept as the singular; set the plural when convenient.
- Rewrote the empty-state description. The old one promised "no more falling behind," which isn't a promise Verso makes or can keep.

### Internal
- `getCollectionTerm`, `singularize`, `capitalize`, `exampleCollectionName` and `addSummaryRow` were each defined separately in up to four classes. They're now single module-level functions.
- Removed unused vocabulary options (`classes`, `subjects`) that no longer appeared in settings, four orphaned CSS rules, and leftover comments from an unrelated plugin.
- Toast styling moved from inline JavaScript into `styles.css`, so themes and snippets can override it.

releases.author: LiveAQuietLife
releases.description:
## [1.0.4] - 2026-07-09

### Fixed
- Finish dates in the past are now blocked when activating a planned book or adding a book in "start reading now" mode, matching the rule Edit Schedule already enforced. Previously, a past finish date would compress the entire book into a single chunk due today with no warning.
- The Start Reading modal now shows inline validation messages below the finish date field, same as Edit Schedule.

### Notes
- Due dates on planned books are intentionally unrestricted — a past due date on a book you haven't started is metadata, not a schedule commitment.
